annotations.keyFindings: Unplanned attendances in the trial week were 11 of 102 before and 12 of 97 after the mid-trial visit became a nurse telephone review; 89 and 91 percent reached the implant decision on the planned day; median nurse time was 18 minutes per call.

annotations.keyFindings: Median round trip 96 km; 58 percent of patients brought a companion, who lost a working day in 41 percent of visits; median out-of-pocket cost 34 per visit.

annotations.keyFindings: Infection in 27 of 1,140 trials (2.4 percent); 21 of the 27 were first noticed after day 5 and 19 were first reported by the patient.
annotations.limitations: Record review across five centres; infection definitions may have differed between centres.

annotations.keyFindings: Satisfaction 8.6 with telephone against 8.8 with face-to-face follow-up, within the non-inferiority margin; unplanned visits 7 against 6 percent; 12 minutes per call against 25 minutes per clinic appointment.
annotations.limitations: Follow-up two weeks after the procedure, not during a trial week; people with hearing impairment or needing an interpreter were excluded.

annotations.keyFindings: Thirteen studies; remote follow-up reduced travel wherever measured; two reported health service costs without an analysis of uncertainty; none took the patient perspective.
annotations.limitations: Mostly historical comparisons at serious risk of bias; search ended in December 2022.

annotations.keyFindings: Telephone review 21, nurse clinic appointment 64 and consultant appointment 148 per contact at 2021 prices; overheads 38 percent of clinic appointment cost.
annotations.limitations: One hospital; prices need uplifting; patient costs excluded.

annotations.keyFindings: A 14-member panel recommends a named contact, a wound check by day 3 in person or by structured remote review, and an in-person review before lead removal; no comparative evidence on timing.
annotations.limitations: Consensus without a systematic evidence review; costs not considered.

claims.text: In one regional service, unplanned attendances during the trial week were 11 of 102 before and 12 of 97 after the mid-trial clinic visit was replaced by a nurse telephone review.
claims.passage: unplanned attendances during the trial week were 11 of 102 before and 12 of 97 after
claims.interpretation: Supports the safety side of the change; an uncontrolled comparison, so it sets expectations rather than an effect size.

claims.text: Of 27 infections in 1,140 spinal cord stimulation trials, 21 were first noticed after day 5 and 19 were first reported by the patient.
claims.passage: Of the 27 infections, 21 were first noticed after day 5 of the trial and 19 were first reported by the patient rather than found at a scheduled visit.
claims.interpretation: A day 3 visit is unlikely to be where infections are found; infections within 30 days belong in the evaluation as a balancing consequence.

claims.text: A nurse-led telephone review cost 21 per contact against 64 for a nurse clinic appointment at 2021 prices.
claims.passage: A nurse-led telephone review cost 21 per contact, a nurse clinic appointment 64 and a consultant appointment 148 at 2021 prices.
claims.interpretation: Planning values for the cost difference; local 2026 unit costs from the finance department replace them in the analysis.

claims.text: Among 214 neuromodulation clinic patients, the median round trip was 96 km and the companion lost a working day in 41 percent of visits.
claims.passage: The median round trip was 96 km and the median time away from home was five and a half hours.
claims.interpretation: Patient and companion costs are large enough that a health-service-only analysis would miss most of the effect of the change.

claims.text: No study in a review of remote follow-up after neuromodulation included an economic evaluation from the patient perspective.
claims.passage: No study included an economic evaluation from the patient perspective.
claims.interpretation: The local evaluation fills a gap rather than repeating existing work.

synthesis: Seven retrieved records, appraised at abstract level. Replacing a mid-trial clinic visit with a structured nurse telephone review was not followed by more unplanned attendances in one before-after evaluation (11 of 102 against 12 of 97), and a randomised trial after interventional procedures found telephone follow-up non-inferior for satisfaction with half the clinician time. Trial infections are usually noticed after day 5 and reported by the patient, so the day 3 visit is not where they are found. A micro-costing study prices a telephone review at about a third of a nurse clinic appointment, and patient travel and companion costs are substantial. No study has combined health service and patient costs with an honest account of uncertainty.
gradeRationale: One uncontrolled before-after evaluation, one randomised trial in a related but different follow-up setting, a review of mostly historical comparisons and single-site costing; consistent in direction but indirect and at risk of bias.
summary: Seven retrieved records appraised; five source-derived claims with passages; overall certainty low.
